faqs.question: What does DotGrey actually do?
faqs.answer: We design and build digital products end to end: product and brand design, websites and apps, custom software, automation and integrations, data pipelines and dashboards, and machine-learning features. Most engagements combine two or three of those in one team.

faqs.question: Who do you usually work with?
faqs.answer: Founders and established teams who need something built properly, or rebuilt because it has outgrown its first version. We are happy to say no when a project is not a fit, and to point you somewhere better.

faqs.question: Where is the team based?
faqs.answer: Our studio is in Dhaka and part of the team works remotely across four time zones. We keep a daily overlap window with every client and agree it at kickoff.

faqs.question: Do you sign NDAs?
faqs.answer: Yes, routinely, and before the first detailed conversation if you prefer. We can work from your template or send ours.

faqs.question: How does a project start?
faqs.answer: A short call, then a written brief we both agree on before any paid work begins. Larger engagements open with a discovery phase to settle scope, risks and how success will be measured.

faqs.question: How will we know how it is going?
faqs.answer: You get a working demo every week and a short written update: what shipped, what is next, and anything at risk. You also have direct access to the people doing the work, not an account layer.

faqs.question: Can you work with our existing code or team?
faqs.answer: Yes. We often join an in-house team, take over a codebase, or extend a system someone else started. We begin with an audit so we know what we are inheriting before we promise anything.

faqs.question: Who owns the work?
faqs.answer: You do. Code, designs, models and documentation transfer to you as the work is paid for, in your repositories and accounts from day one wherever possible.

faqs.question: How do you price projects?
faqs.answer: Fixed price for well-defined scopes such as a discovery sprint or a website, and a monthly team rate for products that evolve. Every proposal states what is included, what is not, and what would change the price.

faqs.question: Do we need a big budget to work with you?
faqs.answer: No. Many relationships start small, with an audit, an automation that saves a team a day a week, or a dashboard that answers one question well. We scope to what moves the needle first.

faqs.question: What happens if the scope changes?
faqs.answer: It usually does. We flag the change as soon as we see it, explain the trade-off in time and cost, and only proceed once you agree in writing.

faqs.question: How do you use AI responsibly?
faqs.answer: We use models where judgement is needed and people where accountability is. Every ML or LLM feature ships with an evaluation set, monitoring and a way for a person to review or override it.

faqs.question: What happens to our data?
faqs.answer: It stays in infrastructure you control or approve. We do not use client data to train third-party models, we document every place data flows, and we follow your security and retention policies.

faqs.question: How do we know if AI is even the right answer?
faqs.answer: We test that first. Often a rule, a better form or a clean data pipeline beats a model. When a model is the right tool, we prove it against a baseline before building around it.

faqs.question: What happens after launch?
faqs.answer: Every engagement includes a support period for fixes. After that, most clients keep a small retainer for improvements, monitoring and updates, or we hand over fully to your team with documentation.

faqs.question: Can our team take it over later?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we plan for it from the start: documented code, a real design system, tests and runbooks, plus handover sessions with your engineers.
